comments.author: _HAVOC_
comments.body_html:
Feedback after quick testing: When I walk across a bridge in daylight, the indicator drops to the halfway mark, as if I were standing in the shade. However, the reading shouldn’t drop, since the lighting conditions haven’t changed. I suspect this is a bug (related to the water surface underneath).

When I hide in a bush, the indicator doesn’t drop. Yet, the light level should decrease, since I’m sitting in the shade or am obscured by foliage. I think this is a bug. To check: (Bushes)

Is vegetation actually taken into account in the mod?

Is it possible to expand the mod to factor in the player’s visible mass?

Example: In reality, it would be incredibly difficult for one person to spot another on a balcony of a building with 30 balconies. It becomes even harder if the person on the balcony is looking out through just a 15cm-wide gap beneath the balcony’s outer wall (e.g., Shoreline - Sanatorium).

Another example: If only half of a player’s face is visible from behind a tree in the forest, opponents will struggle to spot them due to the player’s reduced silhouette.

A small script that accounts for the player’s visible mass and factors it into the visibility calculation:

15% visible mass + 50m distance + lighting conditions = 40% harder to detect.

15% visible mass + 20m distance + same lighting conditions = 10% harder to detect…

Detection is re-checked at 3-second intervals to see if anything has changed—making the opponent easier or harder to spot.

Additionally, a probability factor and a “chance” element could be incorporated so that, even with poor visibility, it sometimes becomes slightly easier to spot opponents—OR to avoid being spotted. Let’s take an example: 15% visible mass + 50m distance + lighting conditions = 40% reduced detectability.

This 40% figure is not fixed; instead, it can vary randomly—ranging from -10% to +20%—each time detection is recalculated.

As mass increases or distance decreases, the probability rises exponentially.

A 80% detection probability isn’t exactly double the base value, but slightly more. This involves an element of “luck” or “bad luck”—much like in real life—depending on whether one happens to look at that specific spot or not. With the base mod, the player now has a chance to remain undetected for varying lengths of time in poor lighting conditions. When the “mass principle” and probability factors are factored in, the situation remains tense, and the player cannot always rely 100% on lighting conditions alone.

The principle works like this: all new values ​​are incorporated into the detection probability (base factors). Added to this are the probability factors (+x% or -x%) detection probability (a baseline range of -10% to +20%)—which also depend on the NPC’s level, is he sprinting or not and so on.
